rationale: The Latin anchors abjicere, dejicere, projicere, ejicere, propellere, repellere all point to forceful throwing away or casting down/out, as confirmed by the Biblical quotation contexts (e.g., "dejecisti eos dum allevarentur" — you cast them down as they were lifted up; "ne projicias me" — cast me not away). While some Latin terms (reprobare, repudiare) carry a sense of rejection, the dominant physical sense of forceful expulsion best matches hurl.v.01 ("throw forcefully"), which captures the violent, directional casting away implied by the compound a-weorpan.
